-77.56880,37.55340.name: Shady Grove Fertility-Richmond
-77.56880,37.55340.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Erika B. Johnston-MacAnanny, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. -43.35011,-21.76095.name: Nidus Medicina Reprodutiva
-43.35011,-21.76095.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. Website: https://clinicanidus.com.br/. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere. No street address resolved, so this point is the city or the country rather than the centre.

46.58544,24.93070.name: National Health Laboratory
46.58544,24.93070.state: 7090 King Abdulaziz Rd, Al Aarid, DISTRICT 13351, Saudi Arabia, Saudi Arabia
46.58544,24.93070.desc: A BSL4 laboratory, planned. Run by Saudi Ministry of Health. It is categorised as a public health laboratory, working on human health. Personnel work in full-body positive-pressure suits with their own air supply. Operational or announced: Announced 2015. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

101.68690,3.13900.name: National Biosafety Board Malaysia
101.68690,3.13900.desc: Malaysia’s biosafety regulator, which approved the release of engineered mosquitoes and requires public consultation on release applications. Its consultation records are published, which makes it one of the few places the public part of a release decision can be examined afterwards.

-83.34900,40.23400.name: Select Sires / bovine genetics cooperatives
-83.34900,40.23400.desc: A farmer-owned cooperative supplying dairy and beef genetics across the United States. Genomic selection has compressed dairy generation intervals sharply, so a trait chosen now reaches a national herd within a few years whether the supplier is a cooperative or a corporation.

-0.12500,51.50100.name: Genetic Technology (Precision Breeding) Act — in force in England
-0.12500,51.50100.desc: Sixty-six UK records sit on this map and none of them recorded the change that matters most: the Act passed in March 2023 came into force on 13 November 2025, its secondary legislation finalised the previous May. It removes plants and animals produced by modern biotechnology, and food and feed derived from them, from GMO regulation where the organism could have occurred naturally or been produced by traditional methods. In their place, two tiers: a marketing notice from Defra, then a food and feed authorisation from the Food Standards Agency, Tier 1 a lighter assessment and Tier 2 a bespoke one. The regulations require the FSA to keep a public food and feed register naming each authorised organism, its reference number, the authorisation-holder, the purpose of the intended genetic change and a safety summary. Two limits: it applies to ENGLAND ONLY, the Scottish and Welsh Parliaments having withheld legislative consent, and the secondary legislation for ANIMALS has not been laid. Commentary describing the reform places England alongside Canada, Australia, Brazil, Argentina, the United States and Japan.
